title: Backups are proven restorable and rollback returns the previous sha
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-7683a432eb3f4e87b1eb0cbc6e3a55ff (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 task-6ec875f4dd5f4f2ab97e46f71bf57b2b for the probe that confirms a rollback actually recovered.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: (a) scheduled BACKUPS of the project store and, per environment with a database, `pg_dump` - written under `<project>/.moe-next/backups/...` with a sha256 and a retention of N; (b) `deployment.rollback {environment, toReceiptRef}` (human-only), redeploying the previous image/sha with an atomic replace and the same health probe, optionally restoring the database backup taken at that deploy. No UI - child 3.

EVERY BACKUP IS PROVEN RESTORABLE. The parent's DoD 2 is unusually strong and correct: a restore-to-temp check whose sha256 is recorded PER RECEIPT. A backup that has never been restored is a file with a hopeful name, and the moment you discover otherwise is the moment you need it. This is the row's central property.

THE BACKUP LOCATION ALREADY HAS A CONVENTION: apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/activation-receipts-measure.ts:32-33 defines BACKUP_DIRECTORY '.moe-next' and BACKUP_LEAF 'backups'. Reuse it - a second backup location is a second place to search during an incident. The migrations row (task-78eedd8ebc2b43c581ac21ea28648a9a, a sibling parent's child) writes `pg_dump` backups to the same tree; coordinate on the layout rather than interleaving two schemes.

ROLLBACK RESOLVES THROUGH THE KEPT DEPLOY RECEIPT that task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5 stores (a SIBLING parent's row - no dependsOn allowed). Build against the shape recorded there. ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING is the case that matters: the receipt names an image that no longer exists locally, and the honest answer is a refusal, not a rebuild from source, which would produce a different image under the same sha.

RETENTION PRUNES, AND THE RECEIPT SAYS WHAT IT PRUNED. Silent deletion of backups is how the one you needed disappears.
definitionOfDone: Scheduled backups write the project store and, per environment with a database, a `pg_dump`, under the EXISTING `.moe-next/backups` convention with a sha256 per backup. Assert the files exist and their recorded sha256 matches the bytes.

EVERY BACKUP IS PROVEN RESTORABLE: a restore-to-temp check runs per backup and its sha256 equality is RECORDED IN THE RECEIPT. Assert a real restore round trip, and assert that a backup which fails to restore is recorded as FAILED rather than kept as a good one - an unrestorable backup that reports success is worse than no backup, because it stops anyone looking for another.

RETENTION PRUNES TO N and the receipt LISTS THE PRUNED REFS. Assert the count after pruning and that the listed refs are the ones actually removed - silent deletion is how the backup you needed disappears.

`deployment.rollback` published HUMAN-ONLY and MCP-EXCLUDED with the full roster backfill and a bidirectional set-equality roster test. Rolling back a production environment is never an agent's decision.

The rollback offline test asserts the PREVIOUS IMAGE TAG is redeployed (resolved from the kept deploy receipt, not rebuilt from source - a rebuild under the same sha produces a different image) and that the DB restore is applied ONLY when requested. Assert the not-requested path leaves the database untouched.
ROLLBACK_RECEIPT_UNKNOWN, ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING and BACKUP_FAILED each assert code + layer. ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING refuses rather than rebuilding.
After a rollback the health probe from child 1 confirms recovery - assert the environment returns to UP through the real probe path, not through an internal flag.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.
taskRails: A BACKUP THAT HAS NEVER BEEN RESTORED IS NOT A BACKUP. The restore-to-temp proof per receipt is this row's reason for existing.
NEVER REBUILD AN IMAGE TO SATISFY A ROLLBACK. A rebuild under the same sha is a different image; a missing image is ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING.
RETENTION NAMES WHAT IT DELETED. Silent pruning loses the one you needed.
REUSE `.moe-next/backups` (activation-receipts-measure.ts:32-33) and coordinate the layout with the migrations row's pg_dump backups - one tree, one scheme.
`deployment.rollback` IS HUMAN-ONLY, and the DB restore happens ONLY when explicitly requested.

implementationPlan.description:
PREREQUISITES, MADE EXPLICIT SO NOBODY RE-PARKS (the governor's third ask).

A. DOCKER. `docker version --format "{{.Server.Version}}"`. At plan time this returned **29.6.2** - the governor started Docker Desktop at 07:42Z and the absent-pipe failure recorded at 22:25Z no longer reproduces. Record the version verbatim.
IF IT FAILS: `moe.report_blocked` with the measurable unblock condition "a running Docker engine; verify with `docker version --format {{.Server.Version}}` returning a version", quoting the failure. Do NOT mock postgres to get past it - DoD 2's restore round trip is the row's reason for existing and a mocked restore proves nothing.

B. THERE ARE NO POSTGRES BINARIES AND THERE WILL NOT BE. Three independent probes agree: `which pg_dump psql` (nothing), `Get-Command psql,pg_dump,pg_restore` (nothing), `wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 --exec sh -c 'command -v psql; command -v pg_dump; command -v pg_restore'` (no output, exit 1). So `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` RUN INSIDE A CONTAINER - `docker run --rm postgres:<tag> pg_dump ...` - never as host binaries. A plan step assuming a host binary is what re-parked this row once.

C. RE-GREP THE EXISTING SEAM BY SYMBOL, NOT BY LINE. The preflight comment's line numbers have drifted (it cited `backupStamp` at :146; it now sits nearer :198). Locate by name in apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/activation-receipts-measure.ts: `backupStamp`, `measureBackup`, `BACKUP_RETENTION`, `pruneBackups`, and `nodeActivationReceiptPorts().backup` in activation-receipts-ports.ts. Record what each currently does.

D. SCOPE CHECK. This row owns DoD 1-3 (backups) ONLY - comment-e4f1db2f: "Where description and plan disagree, THE PLAN IS AUTHORITY." DoD 4-7 belong to task-b22462cf, task-2ab7b462 and task-da60dc4b. Confirm `deployment.rollback` is already on the shared contract and do NOT publish it again: a second publish rotates GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST and invalidates every mirror the task-64d2757c batch just rotated.

MAKE THE BACKUP TREE OWNERSHIP STRUCTURAL, and fix the prune seam DoD 3 names.

Edit `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/activation-receipts-measure.ts`:
1. EXPORT the `.moe-next` / `backups` path constants (currently private) so this row and task-0a56ecee resolve one definition rather than two literals. Rail 4 is "one tree, one scheme"; two copies of a string is how that quietly becomes two trees.
2. ADD THE SUBTREE SEGMENTS per the architect ruling recorded on both rows (comment-6513c210 on task-0a56ecee):
   scheduled     -> `<project>/.moe-next/backups/scheduled/<env>/<ts>.sql` (plus the store backup)
   pre-migration -> `<project>/.moe-next/backups/pre-migration/<env>/<ts>.sql`  (task-0a56ecee's, not written here)
3. `pruneBackups` MUST RETURN THE REFS IT REMOVED AND STOP SWALLOWING FAILURES. Today it does neither, and DoD 3 is precisely about that: "the receipt LISTS THE PRUNED REFS ... silent deletion is how the backup you needed disappears." A prune that fails silently leaves the operator believing retention ran.
4. RETENTION IS SCOPED TO `scheduled/` ONLY. A pre-migration dump is what a failed migration restores FROM; a schedule that prunes it removes the safety net exactly when someone reaches for it.

`BACKUP_RETENTION` is already exported (5 at plan time) - reuse it, do not re-declare a second bound.

Update `activation-receipts-measure.test.ts` in the same diff: existing arms pin the private layout and the swallowing prune, and DoD 3's change makes them wrong rather than merely stale. Find them before editing (`grep -n "backups\|prune\|RETENTION"`).

THE CONTAINERISED POSTGRES PORT. Create `apps/daemon/src/backups/backup-ports.ts` (+ a one-line `.js` bridge - the measured convention in this package).

Declare an INJECTABLE port for `pg_dump` and `pg_restore`, with a production implementation that invokes them INSIDE A CONTAINER: `docker run --rm postgres:<tag> pg_dump ...`. There are no host binaries (step 1B), so this is the only path that works on this machine and it matches how the deployed database itself runs.

INVOCATION DISCIPLINE: bare `docker` under `shell: false` with an argv ARRAY. Never a hard-coded `.cmd` (the measured host returns EINVAL for one under shell:false), never a shell string, never a chain. Pin the postgres image TAG rather than `latest`: a dump taken by one server major and restored by another is a failure mode this row would otherwise discover during an incident.

THE CONNECTION STRING NEVER REACHES A LOG, AN ARGV DUMP OR A RECEIPT (epic rail 3). `pg_dump` accepts a URL on argv, and argv is visible to `docker ps` and to anything that records the command - prefer the environment or a passed file, and say in the note which you used and why. A backup receipt carrying a DSN is a secret in a durable record.

ALSO declare the SQLite store-backup port, reusing `nodeActivationReceiptPorts().backup` rather than writing a second copy path.

Everything the port starts, it stops: `--rm` on every container, and any temp directory removed in a `finally`.

THE SCHEDULED BACKUP SERVICE (DoD 1). Create `apps/daemon/src/backups/scheduled-backup.ts` (+ bridge).

Per run it writes: the PROJECT STORE backup, and per environment WITH A DATABASE a `pg_dump` - both under `backups/scheduled/<env>/<ts>.sql` (and the store's own path), each with a RECORDED SHA256 OVER THE BYTES.

The sha256 is computed from the file as written, not from what was sent to the port. Those differ exactly when something truncated the write, which is the case the hash exists to catch.

An environment with NO database is skipped, not failed - and the receipt says which environments were skipped and why. A silent skip reads as a successful backup of nothing.

BACKUP_FAILED is recorded per environment rather than aborting the whole run: one unreachable database must not cost the other environments their backup that cycle. Assert code and layer, reusing an already-rostered layer literal - introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant, which would demand a security-roster backfill this row does not own.

NO SCHEDULING CODE HERE. The daemon's first recurring loop is task-e651725c's; this exposes a callable entry point that a schedule invokes. Arm no timer.

`wc -l` the file and keep it under 250.

EVERY BACKUP IS PROVEN RESTORABLE (DoD 2) - the row's reason for existing (rail 1).

After writing each backup, RESTORE IT TO A TEMPORARY TARGET and record the result IN THE RECEIPT with its sha256 equality. For postgres that is `pg_restore`/`psql` into a THROWAWAY database in a container; for the SQLite store it is a restore to a temp path and a byte comparison.

A BACKUP THAT FAILS TO RESTORE IS RECORDED **FAILED**, NOT KEPT AS A GOOD ONE. DoD 2 spells out the reason and it is the sharpest sentence in the row: an unrestorable backup that reports success is worse than no backup, because it stops anyone looking for another. So the receipt's success member is written only after the restore proves out.

ASSERT A REAL ROUND TRIP, not a shape: seed a known table and row, back up, restore into a fresh throwaway database, and read the row back. A restore that produces an empty database exits 0 and passes any check that only looks at the exit code.

Assert the FAILED path too, by corrupting a backup's bytes and confirming the receipt records FAILED with its code and layer, and that the file is not presented as restorable.

STOP WHAT YOU START (epic rail 4): every throwaway database, container and temp directory released on EVERY exit path INCLUDING the throwing one - teardown in a `finally`, never after the assertions. Enumerate with `docker ps -a` after the arm and assert nothing of yours survives. This row's neighbours are already blocked on exactly this class of failure.

RETENTION NAMES WHAT IT DELETED (DoD 3, rail 3) - `scheduled-backup.test.ts`.

Write more than `BACKUP_RETENTION` scheduled backups, prune, then assert BOTH halves:
1. the COUNT after pruning equals the bound;
2. the receipt's listed pruned refs ARE THE ONES ACTUALLY REMOVED - compare the listed refs against a directory listing taken before and after, not against what the pruner claimed. DoD 3 says "assert ... that the listed refs are the ones actually removed", and a pruner that reports the wrong refs is indistinguishable from a correct one unless the filesystem is the witness.

ASSERT THE OLDEST GO AND THE NEWEST STAY. A count-only assertion passes for a pruner that deletes the newest - the same trap as a ring buffer evicting the wrong end.

RETENTION MUST NOT REACH `pre-migration/` (the architect ruling, comment-6513c210). Write a pre-migration backup beside the scheduled ones, prune past the bound, and assert the pre-migration file SURVIVES. This is the arm that makes the ruling load-bearing rather than a comment; without it a future refactor collapses the subtrees and nothing goes red until a migration needs its backup.

Assert a prune FAILURE is recorded, not swallowed - make a file undeletable if the platform allows, or inject a failing fs port, and confirm the receipt reports it. The seam swallowed failures before this row touched it.

MUTATE AND CONFIRM RED for the newest-vs-oldest direction and for the pre-migration exclusion; restore each and prove it. The new files are UNTRACKED, so `git diff` certifies nothing - back them up out of tree under %TEMP% suffixed by your worker id and prove restores by SHA256 in a separate call.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW (DoD 8, scoped to this row's DoD 1-3).

GATES - each standalone, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (@moe/daemon is apps/daemon - resolve by PACKAGE NAME).
- `pnpm typecheck`.
- `pnpm test` - state that the root include has NO `apps/**`, so it is not evidence for anything this row owns.
Respect the standing gate-concurrency rule from #general: a full-suite run only when no START is open and free RAM allows, with START/END posted. Prefer the filtered daemon leg.

TEARDOWN AUDIT (epic rail 4): after the suite, `docker ps -a` and a temp-directory listing, quoted. Nothing this row started may survive - containers, throwaway databases, temp dirs. Force an arm to throw and re-check; the failure path is where leaks live.

ADVERSARIAL PASS:
- Does a CONNECTION STRING appear in any argv, log line, receipt or error path? `docker ps` shows argv to anyone on the host, and pg tools echo connection parameters on failure (epic rail 3).
- What happens if two backup runs overlap on one environment? `measureBackup` REFUSES an existing destination - does that surface as BACKUP_FAILED, or as a crash? The stamp is millisecond-precision, so this needs two runs in the same millisecond or a clock that repeats; say which you tested.
- A database that disappears mid-dump; a disk that fills during the restore proof; a container that exits non-zero with an empty dump file. Each must record FAILED rather than a success with a zero-byte artifact.
- Does the sha256 come from the file on disk rather than the buffer sent to the port?
- Did anything touch `deployment.rollback`, the vocabulary, or the contract? `git status --porcelain -- packages/` must be empty - DoD 4-7 are other rows'.

PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: merge-base failures, HEAD failures, subtract, intersect with owned paths; complete only when EMPTY. Disclose foreign red verbatim with paths.

comments.author: architect-b63fabf3
comments.content:
SPLIT FOUR WAYS, AND HALF THE REMAINING WORK IS ALREADY BUILT. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 5 files, all new. Where description and plan disagree, THE PLAN IS AUTHORITY.

## Why it split

The row carried backups, a **new human-only command kind with "the full roster backfill and a bidirectional set-equality roster test"**, and the rollback effect. Measured: `deployment.rollback` = **zero hits** anywhere, while `deployment.deploy`/`deployment.set_target` already sit on the roster. So publishing it is the same shape its sibling just paid for — a 6-file contract slice (the roster line rotates the contract digest, four mirrors, two invisible to every gate but `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`) plus a ~6-file daemon slice. Neither fits with the other, and neither fits with a backup subsystem.

- **task-37a50989** — the contract roster + all four digest mirrors
- **task-b22462cf** — daemon wiring + the operator fence, `dependsOn` the contract row
- **task-da60dc4b** — the rollback **effect**, `dependsOn` the wiring + this row + the probe
- **this row** — backups only: DoD 1, 2, 3

I also **dropped this row's `dependsOn` on the probe row** (task-6ec875f4, PLANNING). Backups need no health probe — checked against all three remaining DoD items. It is claimable now rather than gated behind a PLANNING sibling.

## Half of DoD-1 and DoD-3 already exist

`activation-receipts-measure.ts` already writes the store backup to `.moe-next/backups/<17-digit ms stamp>.sqlite` through a real `node:sqlite` online backup, computes a **sha256**, records `<path>@sha256:<hash>`, refuses to overwrite an existing destination, and prunes to `BACKUP_RETENTION = 5`. A worker reading DoD-1 and DoD-3 cold would rebuild all of it — and collide with the activation path that calls it.

**What is genuinely new:** the *schedule* (today's is activation-triggered), the per-environment `pg_dump`, the restore proof, and a pruning that **names what it deleted** — today's is documented "Housekeeping only" and swallows every failure silently, which is the opposite of DoD-3.

## The existing sha256 is not the restore proof, and it looks like one

It hashes the backup **file's own bytes** — integrity, not loadability. **A truncated sqlite file and a `pg_dump` that failed halfway and exited 0 both hash perfectly.** That gap *is* this row.

So the test that matters plants a corrupt artifact whose **file hash is valid**, and drill (i) makes the proof report VERIFIED without actually restoring: if the arm stays green, it was testing the file hash — which today's code already does — and this row added nothing.

## Three smaller things

- **A healthy-only test proves the happy path.** DoD-2's hard half is that an unrestorable backup is recorded FAILED, not kept as good — a false green stops anyone looking for another copy.
- **Pruning that lists a subset** passes a naive check while losing the record of the rest. Assert set equality both ways.
- **Changing `pruneBackups`' contract touches activation** — its docblock promises the measured receipt survives a pruning failure. Decide deliberately; do not silently break that promise.

If a new receipt is wanted, `publish-receipt-contracts.ts` is the precedent: a versioned `moe-*-receipt/1` under an `internal.*` kind, which needs **no roster backfill** at all.
